description: I’m a high schooler that‘s moderately good at coding! I’m passionate about environmental conservation and would love to create a project catered towards that
summary: WildRoute is a free web map that shows which villages sit closest to the forest edge, where elephants raid crops and people are most at risk. It uses NASA-ISRO NISAR L-band radar, which sees through monsoon cloud, to map the dense forest core and the farmland belts within 0.5 km and 1 km of it. Every settlement is ranked by risk and given practical coexistence actions, such as legal solar fences, lit paths and early warning, plus a draft alert in English and Tamil. It runs across 5 landscapes in India and Sri Lanka. At Mudumalai, tested against 418 GPS-recorded crop raids, the riskiest 20% of land held 71% of raids.
details:
What it does: WildRoute turns NISAR radar into a village-level conflict map. A fixed rule combines protected-forest boundaries with NISAR’s radar forest signal (HV backscatter: forest about −11 dB vs farmland −16 dB) to find the dense forest core. Farmland within 0.5 and 1 km forms the exposure belt, and each settlement gets a risk score that falls with distance from the forest, based on published crop-raid studies.
Benefits and impact: Forest officers and village committees can send fences, patrols and alerts to edge villages first. NISAR revisits every 12 days, so maps can refresh through the monsoon, when optical satellites see only cloud and conflict peaks.
Evidence: At Mudumalai, the riskiest 20% of land held 71% of 418 GPS-recorded raids (ROC-AUC 0.87), with the test design fixed before testing.
Tools: Python (rasterio, numpy, geopandas), Leaflet web map, NISAR GCOV via ASF, 30 m processing; full run in about 8 minutes across 5 landscapes.
Creativity: It uses radar to see where conflict happens rather than only counting incidents, and it turns that into actions and a draft alert in the local language.
Factors considered: village privacy (no names of victims, leopard data no finer than 5 km), animal welfare (no live-wire fences)
